chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Pittsburgh musicians: Toodle-oo and Boots Swan
summary: She remembers boogie-woogie pianists and Boots Swan, the most popular singer, who never recorded.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, there's a whole list of great musicians from Pittsburgh is endless.
Let me pick out a couple of not

so well known ones which I have taken from the book of There was a Boogie Woogie piano player. Nobody is quite sure what his first name was, but one possibility is that it was Toodle-oo.

I remember having seen Toodle-oo around Pittsburgh working in some little club but he would be one of the musicians I met at the Crawford Grill or at the musician's club. And the other one was "Dry Bread". Yeah, I remember him. And I remember "Dry Bread". And there were other entertainers around Pittsburgh too that were lined up at the Crawford Grill.
Did you hear them play ever?
What kind of style did they play?
I would say that they were playing, more or less, boogie-woogie, you know, real jazz. There were entertainers that would show up, Boots Swan was the . . .
Boots Swan. She was the most popular singer around Pittsburgh. She was the competition that nobody could get a job around Boots Swan. She

had a very big voice. And then there were . . .
Do you know what happened to her?
Yeah, she was around Pittsburgh for years up until the time she died, I guess. But she worked in some of the clubs, the big cabarets they had there. She didn't need a microphone.
Did she record as far as you know?

No, I don't think Boots ever made any recordings. I don't know why, but she was a very big singer, had a very big voice. And she didn't just stick to blues either. I mean, she sang currently popular tunes. She might have had a few specialty songs that she did. The girls in the chorus that was in some of these clubs, they would come up to the Crawford Grill and the musicians, and they would perform. So anyway, the local bands around, I saw all the musicians when we wound up at the club.
